[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Kubernetes Services: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, and ExternalName"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In Kubernetes, Pods are mortal. They are created and destroyed to match the desired state of your cluster. While a Pod has its own IP address, that IP is not permanent. This creates a challenge: how do you reliably route traffic to a changing set of Pods? The answer is a Kubernetes Service."},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Kubernetes Service is an abstract way to expose an application running on a set of Pods as a network service. Kubernetes provides four main types of Services to handle different networking topologies and traffic routing requirements."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"1. ClusterIP (Default)"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"ClusterIP is the default and most common service type. It exposes the service on an internal IP address that is only reachable from within the cluster. This is ideal for internal microservices that do not need to be accessed from the outside world."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-internal-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: MyApp
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. NodePort"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"NodePort exposes the service on a static port on each worker node's IP address (typically in the range 30000-32767). Any traffic sent to this port on any node is automatically forwarded to the corresponding Service and Pods."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-nodeport-service
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: MyApp
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
      nodePort: 30007"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. LoadBalancer"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The LoadBalancer service type is the standard way to expose your services to the internet. It provisions an external load balancer (such as AWS ELB or Google Cloud Load Balancer) in cloud environments, automatically routing external traffic to the NodePort and ClusterIP services underneath."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-loadbalancer-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: MyApp
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. ExternalName"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"ExternalName services are a special case. They do not have selectors and do not define any ports or endpoints. Instead, they map a Service to a DNS name, allowing pods to access external resources (like a database hosted outside the cluster) using standard internal DNS names."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-external-service
  namespace: default
spec:
  type: ExternalName
  externalName: my.database.external.com"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Service Types"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ClusterIP: Internal cluster communication only."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"NodePort: Exposes services on a static port across all cluster nodes."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LoadBalancer: Integrates with cloud providers to provision external load balancers."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ExternalName: Maps services to external DNS names without proxying."}]
